articleTitle: The Ext Algebra and a New Generalization of D-Koszul Algebras
abstract: We generalize Koszul and D-Koszul algebras by introducing a class of graded algebras called (D, A)-stacked algebras. We give a characterization of (D, A)-stacked algebras, and show that their Ext algebra is finitely generated as an algebra in degrees 0, 1, 2 and 3. In the monomial case, we give an explicit description of the Ext algebra by quiver and relations, and show that the ideal of relations has a quadratic Gröbner basis; this enables us to give a regrading of the Ext algebra under which the regraded Ext algebra is a Koszul algebra.

articleTitle: On the h-invariant of Cubic Forms, and Systems of Cubic Forms
abstract: We define a so-called ℓ-invariant for systems of homogeneous forms of the same degree, which coincides with the well-known h-invariant for a single quadratic or cubic form, and bound the ℓ-invariant of a system of rational forms <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F_1,\dots,F_r$</tex> in terms of the ℓ-invariant of a single form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha_1F_1+\dots+\alpha_rF_r$</tex> in their complex pencil in case of algebraic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_r$</tex>. As an application, we show that a system of r rational cubic forms in more than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4000\ 000r^4$</tex> variables has a non-trivial rational zero.

articleTitle: A C*-Algebra Version of Kolmogolov's Factorization Theorem
abstract: Let G be a Hausdorff space. We introduce the notion of a positive definite function from G × G into an abstract C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>-algebra, and we show that for a continuous positive definite function K from G × G into a C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>-algebra A, there exist a Hilbert A-module X with A-valued inner product <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\langle \cdot,\cdot\rangle$</tex> and a continuous function T from G into X such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$K(s,t)=\langle T(s),T(t)\rangle\quad{\rm for\ all}\ s,t\in G.$$</tex>

articleTitle: On Coincidences Among Quadratic Fields Generated by the Shanks Sequence
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g\gt1$</tex> be an integer and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f(X)\in \mathbb Z[X]$</tex> a polynomial of positive degree with no multiple roots, and put <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u(n)=f\ (g^n)$</tex>. In this note, we study the sequence of quadratic fields <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb Q(\sqrt{u(n)})$</tex> as n varies over the consecutive integers <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M+1,\dots,M+N$</tex>. Fields of this type include Shanks fields and their generalizations. Using the square sieve together with new bounds on character sums, we improve an upper bound of Luca and Shparlinski (Proc. Edinb. Math. Soc. (2) 52 (2009), 3) on the number of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\in\{M+1,\dots,M+N\}$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb Q\sqrt {u(n)}=\mathbb Q(\sqrt {s})$</tex> for a given squarefree integer s.

articleTitle: On reducible and primitive subsets of ${\mathbb{F}^p}$P, II
abstract: In Part I of this paper, we introduced and studied the notion of reducibility and primitivity of subsets of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb {F}_p$</tex>: a set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal {A} \subset \mathbb {F}_p$</tex> is said to be reducible if it can be represented in the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal {A} = \mathcal {B} + \mathcal {C}$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal {B}, \mathcal {C} \subset \mathbb {F}_p$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|\mathcal {B}|, |\mathcal {C}| \geqslant 2$</tex>; if there are no such sets <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal {B}, \mathcal {C}$</tex>, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal {A}$</tex> is said to be primitive. Here, we introduce and study a strong form of primitivity and reducibility: a set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal {A} \subset \mathbb {F}_p$</tex> is said to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-primitive if changing at most <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> elements of it we always get a primitive set, and it is said to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-reducible if it has a representation in the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal {A} = \mathcal {B}_1 + \mathcal {B}_2 + \cdots + \mathcal {B}_k$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal {B}_1, \mathcal {B}_2, \ldots , \mathcal {B}_k \subset \mathbb {F}_p$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|\mathcal {B}_1|, |\mathcal {B}_2|, \ldots , |\mathcal {B}_k| \geqslant 2$</tex>.

articleTitle: Exact Additive Complements
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${A,B}$</tex> be sets of positive integers such that A + B contains all but finitely many positive integers. Sárközy and Szemerédi proved that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A(x)B(x)/x \rightarrow 1$</tex>, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A(x)B(x)-x \rightarrow \infty$</tex>. Chen and Fang considerably improved Sárközy and Szemerédi's bound. We further improve their estimate and show by an example that our result is nearly best possible.

articleTitle: Idempotent States on Locally Compact Quantum Groups II
abstract: Correspondence between idempotent states and expected right-invariant subalgebras is extended to non-coamenable, non-unimodular locally compact quantum groups; in particular left convolution operators are shown to automatically preserve the right Haar weight.

articleTitle: Gaps between fractional parts, and additive combinatorics
abstract: We give bounds on the number of distinct differences <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf N_a-a$</tex> as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex> varies over all elements of a given finite set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A\subseteq (\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^d$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d\geq 1$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf N_a$</tex> is a nearest neighbour to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex>.

articleTitle: A low-energy decomposition theorem
abstract: We prove that any finite set of real numbers can be split into two parts, one part being highly non-additive and the other highly non-multiplicative.

articleTitle: Sárközy's Theorem in Function Fields
abstract: Sárközy proved that dense sets of integers contain two elements differing by a kth power. The bounds in quantitative versions of this theorem are rather weak compared with what is expected. We prove a version of Sárközy's theorem for polynomials over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{F}_q}$</tex> with polynomial dependencies in the parameters. More precisely, let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${P_{q,n}}$</tex> be the space of polynomials over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{F}_q}$</tex> of degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\lt n}$</tex> in an indeterminate T. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${k\geq 2}$</tex> be an integer and let q be a prime power. Set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${c(k,q):=(2k^{2}D_q(k)^{2}log q)^{-1}}{\rm Where} D_q(k)$</tex>, where D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</inf>(k) is the sum of the digits of k in base q. If <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${A\subset p_{q,n}}$</tex> is a set with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${|A|\gt 2q^{1-(k,q))}}$</tex> such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${p(T) - p^{'}(T) = b(T)^k {\rm for som} b\epsilon \mathbb{F_q[T]}}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Effectively Computing Integral Points on the Moduli of Smooth Quartic Curves
abstract: We prove an effective version of the Shafarevich conjecture (as proven by Faltings) for smooth quartic curves in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{P}^\mathit2$</tex>. To do so, we establish an effective version of Scholl's finiteness result for smooth del Pezzo surfaces of degree at most 4.

articleTitle: o-minimal Flows on Abelian Varieties
abstract: Let A be an abelian variety over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{C}}$</tex> of dimension n and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\pi: \mathbb{C}\rightarrow A}$</tex> be the complex uniformization. Let X be an unbounded subset of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\pi: \mathbb{C}\rightarrow A}$</tex> definable in a suitable o-minimal structure. We give a description of the Zariski closure of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{C}^{n}}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Quadratic residues and difference sets
abstract: It has been conjectured by Sárközy that with finitely many exceptions, the set of quadratic residues modulo a prime <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> cannot be represented as a sumset <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\{a+b\colon a\in A, b\in B\}$</tex> with non-singleton <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A,B\subseteq {\mathbb F}_p$</tex>. The case <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A=B$</tex> of this conjecture has been recently established by Shkredov. The analogous problem for differences remains open: is it true that, for all sufficiently large primes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>, the set of quadratic residues modulo <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> is not of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\{a'-a''\colon a',a''\in A,\,a'\ne a''\}$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A\subseteq {\mathbb F}_p$</tex>? We attack here a presumably more tractable variant of this problem, which is to show that there is no <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A\subseteq {\mathbb F}_p$</tex> such that every quadratic residue has a unique representation as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a'-a''$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a',a''\in A$</tex>, and no non-residue is represented in this form. We give a number of necessary conditions for the existence of such <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>, involving for the most part the behavior of primes dividing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p-1$</tex>. These conditions enable us to rule out all primes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> in the range <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$13<p<10^{20}$</tex> (the primes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p=5$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p=13$</tex> being conjecturally the only exceptions).

articleTitle: Ramsey multiplicity of linear patterns in certain finite abelian groups
abstract: In this article, we explore an arithmetic analogue of a long-standing open problem in graph theory: what can be said about the number of monochromatic additive configurations in 2-colourings of finite abelian groups? We are able to answer several instances of this question using techniques from additive combinatorics and quadratic Fourier analysis. However, the main purpose of this paper is to advertise this sphere of problems and to put forward a number of concrete questions and conjectures.

articleTitle: ℓ2-TORSION OF FREE-BY-CYCLIC GROUPS
abstract: We provide an upper bound on the ℓ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-torsion of a free-by-cyclic group, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-\rho^{(2)}(\mathbb F\ \rtimes_\Phi\ \mathbb Z)$</tex>, in terms of a relative train-track representative for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Phi\in {\rm Aut}(\mathbb F)$</tex>. Our result shares features with a theorem of Lück–Schick computing the ℓ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-torsion of the fundamental group of a 3-manifold that fibers over the circle in that it shows that the ℓ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-torsion is determined by the exponential dynamics of the monodromy. In light of the result of Lück–Schick, a special case of our bound is analogous to the bound on the volume of a 3-manifold that fibers over the circle with pseudo-Anosov monodromy by the normalized entropy recently demonstrated by Kojima–McShane.

articleTitle: Planar subsets with small doubling
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A,\,B\subseteq {\mathbb Z}^2$</tex> be finite, non-empty subsets each covered by precisely two horizontal lines. Suppose <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \langle A+B-A-B \rangle = {\mathbb Z}^2$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|A|\geq |B|$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|A+B|=|A|+2|B|-3+r\leq |A|+\frac {19}{7}|B|-5$</tex>. Then there exist subsets <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P_A,P_B,P\subseteq {\mathbb Z}^2$</tex>, each the union of two arithmetic progressions with difference <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(1,0)$</tex>, such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A\subseteq P_A$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B\subseteq P_B$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(x+A)\cup (y+B)\subseteq P$</tex>, for some <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x,y\in {\mathbb Z}^2$</tex>, with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|P_A|\leq |A|+r$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|P _B|\leq |B|+r$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|P_A|+|P_B|\leq 2|B|+2r$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|P|\leq {(|A|+|B|)}/{2}+\frac 32r$</tex>. A similar result is proved assuming that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> is covered by two horizontal lines and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B$</tex> by one and vice versa. This generalizes a result of Stanchescu handling the case <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A=B$</tex> and extends the Freiman <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3k-4$</tex> Theorem to two-dimensional sumsets with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|A+B|< |A|+\frac 73|B|-5$</tex>.

articleTitle: Solving xz = y2 in Certain Subsets of Finite Groups
abstract: Suppose that G is a finite group and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${A\subset G}$</tex> has no non-trivial solutions to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${xz =y^{2}}$</tex>. if there is a triple<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${(x, y, z)\in A^3}$</tex> such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$xz = y2;$</tex>We shall show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${xz =y^{2}}$</tex> we say that the solution is non-trivial if<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$xz = y2;$</tex> This paper is concerned with the following result of Bergelson, McCutcheon and Zhang..

articleTitle: Multiple point spaces of finite holomorphic maps
abstract: Given a finite holomorphic map <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f\mathit:X\mathit\rightarrow Y$</tex> between manifolds, we show that there exists a unique possible definition of kth multiple point space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${D^{k}(F)}$</tex> with the following properties: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${D^{k}(F)}$</tex> is a closed subspace of X<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sup>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${D^{k}(F)}$</tex> is the closure of the set of strict k-multiple points when f is stable and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${D^{k}(F)}$</tex> is well behaved under deformations. Our construction coincides with Mond's double point space and Mond's kth multiple point space for corank one singularities. We also give some interesting properties of the double point space and prove that in many cases it can be computed as the zero locus of the quotient of ideals <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${(f\times f )^{*}\mathscr I_{\triangle(Y)}:\mathscr I_{\triangle(X)}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr I_{\triangle(Z)}$</tex> is the defining ideal sheaf of the diagonal in Z × Z.

articleTitle: Sign Changing Solutions for Quasilinear Superlinear Elliptic Problems
abstract: Results on existence and multiplicity of solutions for a nonlinear elliptic problem driven by the Φ-Laplace operator are established. We employ minimization arguments on suitable Nehari manifolds to build a negative and a positive ground state solutions. In order to find a nodal solution we employ additionally the well-known Deformation lemma and Topological Degree Theory.

articleTitle: Coideals, Quantum Subgroups and Idempotent States
abstract: We establish a one-to-one correspondence between idempotent states on a locally compact quantum group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{G}$</tex> and integrable coideals in the von Neumann algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^\infty(\mathbb G)$</tex> that are preserved by the scaling group. In particular, we show that there is a one-to-one correspondence between idempotent states on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb G$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\psi_\mathbb G$</tex>-expected left-invariant von Neumann subalgebras of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^\infty(\mathbb G)$</tex>. We characterize idempotent states of Haar type as those corresponding to integrable normal coideals preserved by the scaling group. We also establish a one-to-one correspondence between open subgroups of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb G$</tex> and central idempotent states on the dual <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widehat {\mathbb G}$</tex>. Finally, we characterize coideals corresponding to open quantum subgroups of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb G$</tex> as those that are normal and admit an atom. As a byproduct of this study, we get a number of universal lifting results for Podleś condition, normality and regularity, and we generalize a number of results known before to hold under the coamenability assumption.

articleTitle: Inverse theorems for sets and measures of polynomial growth
abstract: We give a structural description of the finite subsets <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> of an arbitrary group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> which obey the polynomial growth condition <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|A^n| \leq n^d |A|$</tex> for some bounded <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex> and sufficiently large <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>, showing that such sets are controlled by (a bounded number of translates of) a coset nilprogression in a certain precise sense. This description recovers some previous results of Breuillard–Green–Tao and Breuillard–Tointon concerning sets of polynomial growth; we are also able to describe the subsequent growth of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|A^m|$</tex> fairly explicitly for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m \geq n$</tex>, at least when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> is a symmetric neighbourhood of the identity. We also obtain an analogous description of symmetric probability measures <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu $</tex> whose <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-fold convolutions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu ^{*n}$</tex> obey the condition <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\| \mu ^{*n} \|_{\ell ^2}^{-2} \leq n^d \|\mu \|_{\ell ^2}^{-2}$</tex>. In the abelian case, this description recovers the inverse Littlewood–Offord theorem of Nguyen–Vu, and gives a ‘symmetrized’ variant of a recent non-abelian inverse Littlewood–Offord theorem of Tiep–Vu. Our main tool to establish these results is the inverse theorem of Breuillard, Green, and the author that describes the structure of approximate groups.

articleTitle: The Critical CoHA of a Quiver With Potential
abstract: Pursuing the similarity between the Kontsevich–Soibelman construction of the cohomological Hall algebra (CoHA) of BPS states and Lusztig's construction of canonical bases for quantum enveloping algebras, and the similarity between the integrality conjecture for motivic Donaldson–Thomas invariants and the PBW theorem for quantum enveloping algebras, we build a coproduct on the CoHA associated to a quiver with potential. We also prove a cohomological dimensional reduction theorem, further linking a special class of CoHAs with Yangians, and explaining how to connect the study of character varieties with the study of CoHAs.

articleTitle: Lower bounds for the variance of sequences in arithmetic progressions: Primes and divisor functions
abstract: We develop a general method for lower bounding the variance of sequences in arithmetic progressions mod <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>, summed over all <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q \leq Q$</tex>, building on previous work of Liu, Perelli, Hooley and others. The proofs lower bound the variance by the minor arc contribution in the circle method, which we lower bound by comparing with suitable auxiliary exponential sums that are easier to understand. As an application, we prove a lower bound of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(1-\epsilon ) QN\log (Q^2/N)$</tex> for the variance of the von Mangoldt function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\Lambda (n))_{n=1}^{N}$</tex>, on the range <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sqrt {N} (\log N)^C \leq Q \leq N$</tex>. Previously, such a result was only available assuming the Riemann Hypothesis. We also prove a lower bound <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gg _{k,\delta } Q N (\log N)^{k^2 - 1}$</tex> for the variance of the divisor functions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_k(n)$</tex>, valid on the range <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N^{1/2+\delta } \leq Q \leq N$</tex> for any natural number <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k \geq 2$</tex>.

articleTitle: Lines on K3 Quartic Surfaces in Characteristic 2
abstract: We prove that a K3 quartic surface defined over a field of characteristic 2 can contain at most 68 lines. If it contains 68 lines, then it is projectively equivalent to a member of a one-dimensional family found by Rams and Schütt.

articleTitle: Weakly mixing sets of integers and polynomial equations
abstract: We investigate polynomial patterns which can be guaranteed to appear in weakly mixing sets introduced by Furstenberg and studied by Fish. In particular, we prove that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr {A}$</tex> is a weakly mixing set and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p(x) \in \mathbb {Z}[x]$</tex> is a polynomial of odd degree with positive leading coefficient, then all sufficiently large integers <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> can be represented as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N = n_1 + n_2$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p(n_1) + m,\ p(n_2) + m \in \mathscr {A}$</tex> for some <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m \in \mathscr {A}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Freiman Homomorphisms on Sparse Random Sets
abstract: A result of Fiz Pontiveros shows that if A is a random subset of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{Z}_N$</tex> where each element is chosen independently with probability <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${N^1/2+_o(1)}$</tex>, then with high probability every Freiman homomorphism defined on A can be extended to a Freiman homomorphism on the whole of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{Z}_N$</tex>. In this paper, we improve the bound to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${CN^2/3(log N)^1/3}$</tex>, which is best possible up to the constant factor.

articleTitle: Zero-Density Estimates for Epstein Zeta Functions
abstract: We investigate the zeros of Epstein zeta functions associated with a positive definite quadratic form with rational coefficients in the vertical strip <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma_\mathit1\mathit \il \mathfrak Rs\mathit \lt \sigma_\mathit2$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1/2\lt \sigma_1\lt \sigma_2 \lt$</tex>. When the class number of the quadratic form is bigger than 1, Voronin gives a lower bound and Lee gives an asymptotic formula for the number of zeros. In this paper, we improve their results by providing a new upper bound for the error term.

articleTitle: Symmetric Self-Adjoint Hopf Categories and a Categorical Heisenberg Double
abstract: Motivated by the work of A. Zelevinsky on positive self-adjoint Hopf (PSH) algebras, we define what we call a symmetric self-adjoint Hopf (SSH) structure for a certain kind of semisimple abelian categories. It is known that every PSH algebra admits a natural action of the associated Heisenberg double. We construct canonical morphisms lifting the relations that define this action on the algebra level, and define an object that we call a categorical Heisenberg double that is a natural setting for considering these morphisms. As examples, we exhibit the SSH structure on the categories of polynomial functors and equivariant polynomial functors. In the case of the category of polynomial functors, we obtain categorification of the Fock space representation of the infinite-dimensional Heisenberg algebra.
